Coming to a concert
New York City

Classical concerts in New York.

CreArtBox is a chamber music ensemble founded in New York in 2013. Its New York Series runs from autumn to spring at The DiMenna Center for Classical Music, in Midtown Manhattan, and the four productions of this season each start at 7:30 pm. The calendar says what is on. This page is the practical half: the hall, the way in, how long an evening lasts and what a seat costs.

See the calendar → Tickets are sold through Eventbrite, from the page of each concert.

The hall.

The New York Series is given at The DiMenna Center for Classical Music, 450 West 37th Street, between Ninth and Tenth Avenues in Midtown Manhattan. It is a hall built for classical music, and it is where the ensemble gives its New York Series.

By subway, the A, C and E stop at 34th Street–Penn Station and the 7 at 34th Street–Hudson Yards, both a few minutes' walk. For group rates, accessibility or press tickets, write to info@creartbox.nyc.

The evening.

A CreArtBox programme puts the standard repertoire and new music in the same hour. In the 2026/27 season Brahms and both Schumanns share an evening with Eric Moe; Stravinsky shares one with the world premiere of Hannah Selin's Tectonic Lullaby; and one production, Pressure and Release, is given over entirely to seven composers chosen through the ensemble's open call for scores. Eleven works this season arrived that way.

Most productions carry something besides the music: video art, stage design or lighting made for the room. Currents, on 30 October 2026, runs about an hour and is played without an intermission.

Before you come

Questions we are asked.

Where does CreArtBox perform in New York?

At The DiMenna Center for Classical Music, 450 West 37th Street, between Ninth and Tenth Avenues in Midtown Manhattan. The whole New York Series is given there. The ensemble also tours, and those dates are on the calendar with their own venues.

How do I get to The DiMenna Center?

By subway, the A, C and E stop at 34th Street–Penn Station and the 7 at 34th Street–Hudson Yards; both are a few minutes' walk. The entrance is on West 37th Street.

What time do concerts start?

The four New York Series productions of the 2026/27 season each start at 7:30 pm. Touring dates and Festival ADAR keep their own times, which are on each concert page.

How much are tickets?

Seats are sold through Eventbrite and each concert page carries its own link and prices. Currents, on 30 October 2026, starts at $15. A Premium ticket puts you in the closest rows to the players, with a small treat on the night.

How long is a concert, and is there an intermission?

Currents runs about an hour and is played without an intermission. Running times are given on the concert page once the programme is set.

What kind of music will I hear?

Chamber music, with the standard repertoire and new work in the same evening: in 2026/27, Brahms and both Schumanns share a programme with Eric Moe, and Stravinsky shares one with the world premiere of Hannah Selin's Tectonic Lullaby. Eleven works this season reached the programme through the ensemble's open call for scores. Most productions carry something besides the music, usually video art or stage design made for the room.

Who plays?

The core ensemble is flute, violin, viola, cello and piano – Guillermo Laporta, Emilie-Anne Gendron, Matthew Cohen, Julia Yang and Josefina Urraca – with guest musicians when a programme asks for them. Each concert page lists who is playing that night.

Can I see what CreArtBox has played before?

Yes. The archive holds every performance since 2013, with programmes and photographs, and the repertoire page lists every work the ensemble has played.
